page_title: Some ways to get better at debugging

sources.entry: Some ways to get better at debugging, Julia Evans

summary.title: Some ways to get better at debugging
summary.one_liner: Five categories of debugging skill (codebase, system, tools, strategies, experience), adapted from a troubleshooting paper, that you can deliberately work on to get better at debugging.
keywords: how to get better at debugging
takeaways: Debugging skill can be grouped into five categories: codebase knowledge, system/domain knowledge, tools, strategies, and experience.
Debugging is one of the best ways to learn how an unfamiliar codebase works.
Systems knowledge such as HTTP caching, CORS, and database transactions often needs deliberate study.
Learning tools like debuggers, profilers, strace, tcpdump, and reading error messages well improves debugging.
Experts form more correct hypotheses and find faults faster mainly because of accumulated experience.
summary.summary: Julia Evans shares a framework from the academic paper 'Learning to Troubleshoot: A New Theory-Based Design Architecture' (via 'Towards a framework for teaching debugging'), which splits debugging knowledge into five categories. She reframes each as an action: learn the codebase (system knowledge), learn the system and its surrounding environment (domain knowledge), learn your tools (procedural knowledge), learn strategies (strategic knowledge), and get experience (experiential knowledge). Each section gives short examples, such as HTTP caching for backend work or gdb and tcpdump for tools. The post is brief and informal, and it notes the strategies section is saved for her upcoming debugging zine.
